corrected_asr_transcription: I think I have felt that you were coming.

asr_transcription.text: Alexander flushed angrily.

reference_transcription: ALEXANDER FLUSHED ANGRILY
corrected_asr_transcription: Alexander flushed angrily.

asr_transcription.text: I've been up in Canada with my bridge and I arranged not to come to New York until after you had gone.

reference_transcription: I'VE BEEN UP IN CANADA WITH MY BRIDGE AND I ARRANGED NOT TO COME TO NEW YORK UNTIL AFTER YOU HAD GONE
corrected_asr_transcription: I've been up in Canada with my bridge and I arranged not to come to New York until after you had gone.

asr_transcription.text: Then you don't know what you're talking about.

reference_transcription: THEN YOU DON'T KNOW WHAT YOU'RE TALKING ABOUT
corrected_asr_transcription: Then you don't know what you're talking about.

asr_transcription.text: Yes, I know very well.

reference_transcription: YES I KNOW VERY WELL
corrected_asr_transcription: Yes, I know very well.

asr_transcription.text: I don't know what I ought to say, but I don't believe you'd be happy, truly I don't. Aren't you trying to frighten me?

reference_transcription: I DON'T KNOW WHAT I OUGHT TO SAY BUT I DON'T BELIEVE YOU'D BE HAPPY TRULY I DON'T AREN'T YOU TRYING TO FRIGHTEN ME
corrected_asr_transcription: I don't know what I ought to say, but I don't believe you'd be happy. Truly, I don't. Aren't you trying to frighten me?

asr_transcription.text: The last two days of the voyage Bartley found almost intolerable.

reference_transcription: THE LAST TWO DAYS OF THE VOYAGE BARTLEY FOUND ALMOST INTOLERABLE
corrected_asr_transcription: The last two days of the voyage, Bartley found almost intolerable.

asr_transcription.text: She blushed and smiled and fumbled his card in her confusion before she ran upstairs.

reference_transcription: SHE BLUSHED AND SMILED AND FUMBLED HIS CARD IN HER CONFUSION BEFORE SHE RAN UPSTAIRS
corrected_asr_transcription: She blushed and smiled and fumbled his card in her confusion before she ran upstairs.

asr_transcription.text: The room was empty when he entered.

reference_transcription: THE ROOM WAS EMPTY WHEN HE ENTERED
corrected_asr_transcription: The room was empty when he entered.

asr_transcription.text: Emerging at Houston at half past three o'clock in the afternoon, Alexander had his luggage sent to the Savoy and drove at once to bed for its square.

reference_transcription: EMERGING AT EUSTON AT HALF PAST THREE O'CLOCK IN THE AFTERNOON ALEXANDER HAD HIS LUGGAGE SENT TO THE SAVOY AND DROVE AT ONCE TO BEDFORD SQUARE
corrected_asr_transcription: Emerging at Houston at half past three o'clock in the afternoon, Alexander had his luggage sent to the Savoy and drove at once to Bedford Square.

asr_transcription.text: A coal fire was crackling in the grate and the lamps were lit for it was already beginning to grow dark outside.

reference_transcription: A COAL FIRE WAS CRACKLING IN THE GRATE AND THE LAMPS WERE LIT FOR IT WAS ALREADY BEGINNING TO GROW DARK OUTSIDE
corrected_asr_transcription: A coal fire was crackling in the grate and the lamps were lit, for it was already beginning to grow dark outside.

asr_transcription.text: She merely brushed his cheek with her lips and put a hand lightly and joyously on either shoulder.

reference_transcription: SHE MERELY BRUSHED HIS CHEEK WITH HER LIPS AND PUT A HAND LIGHTLY AND JOYOUSLY ON EITHER SHOULDER
corrected_asr_transcription: She merely brushed his cheek with her lips and put a hand lightly and joyously on either shoulder.

asr_transcription.text: I never dreamed it would be you, Bartley.

reference_transcription: I NEVER DREAMED IT WOULD BE YOU BARTLEY
corrected_asr_transcription: I never dreamed it would be you, Bartley.

asr_transcription.text: She called his name on the threshold, but in her swift flight across the room she felt a change in him and caught herself up so definitely that he could not tell just when she did it.

reference_transcription: SHE CALLED HIS NAME ON THE THRESHOLD BUT IN HER SWIFT FLIGHT ACROSS THE ROOM SHE FELT A CHANGE IN HIM AND CAUGHT HERSELF UP SO DEFTLY THAT HE COULD NOT TELL JUST WHEN SHE DID IT
corrected_asr_transcription: She called his name on the threshold, but in her swift flight across the room she felt a change in him and caught herself up so deftly that he could not tell just when she did it.

asr_transcription.text: She looked at his heavy shoulders and big determined head, first forward like a catapult in leash.

reference_transcription: SHE LOOKED AT HIS HEAVY SHOULDERS AND BIG DETERMINED HEAD THRUST FORWARD LIKE A CATAPULT IN LEASH
corrected_asr_transcription: She looked at his heavy shoulders and big determined head, thrust forward like a catapult in leash.

asr_transcription.text: When did you come, Bartley, and how did it happen? You haven't spoken a word.

reference_transcription: WHEN DID YOU COME BARTLEY AND HOW DID IT HAPPEN YOU HAVEN'T SPOKEN A WORD
corrected_asr_transcription: When did you come, Bartley, and how did it happen? You haven't spoken a word.

asr_transcription.text: I'll do anything you wish me to, Bartley. She said chummylessly.

reference_transcription: I'LL DO ANYTHING YOU WISH ME TO BARTLEY SHE SAID TREMULOUSLY
corrected_asr_transcription: I'll do anything you wish me to, Bartley, she said charmingly.

asr_transcription.text: Always, but it's worse now.

reference_transcription: ALWAYS BUT IT'S WORSE NOW
corrected_asr_transcription: Always, but it's worse now.

asr_transcription.text: He pulled up a window as if the air were heavy.

reference_transcription: HE PULLED UP A WINDOW AS IF THE AIR WERE HEAVY
corrected_asr_transcription: He pulled up a window as if the air were heavy.

asr_transcription.text: It's unbearable. It tortures me every minute.

reference_transcription: IT'S UNBEARABLE IT TORTURES ME EVERY MINUTE
corrected_asr_transcription: It's unbearable. It tortures me every minute.

asr_transcription.text: It hasn't always made you miserable, has it?

reference_transcription: IT IT HASN'T ALWAYS MADE YOU MISERABLE HAS IT
corrected_asr_transcription: It hasn't always made you miserable, has it?

asr_transcription.text: There is this deception between me and everything.

reference_transcription: THERE IS THIS DECEPTION BETWEEN ME AND EVERYTHING
corrected_asr_transcription: There is this deception between me and everything.

asr_transcription.text: Hilda watched him from her corner, trembling and scarcely breathing, dark shadows going about her eyes.

reference_transcription: HILDA WATCHED HIM FROM HER CORNER TREMBLING AND SCARCELY BREATHING DARK SHADOWS GROWING ABOUT HER EYES
corrected_asr_transcription: Hilda watched him from her corner, trembling and scarcely breathing, dark shadows gathering about her eyes.

asr_transcription.text: I get nothing but misery out of either.

reference_transcription: I GET NOTHING BUT MISERY OUT OF EITHER
corrected_asr_transcription: I get nothing but misery out of either.

asr_transcription.text: At that word, deception, spoken with such self-contempt, the color flashed back into Hildesface, as suddenly as if she had been struck by a whip flash.

reference_transcription: AT THAT WORD DECEPTION SPOKEN WITH SUCH SELF CONTEMPT THE COLOR FLASHED BACK INTO HILDA'S FACE AS SUDDENLY AS IF SHE HAD BEEN STRUCK BY A WHIPLASH
corrected_asr_transcription: At that word, deception, spoken with such self-contempt, the color flashed back into Hildes' face, as suddenly as if she had been struck by a whip lash.

asr_transcription.text: I am not a man who can live two lives he went on feverishly. Each life spoils the other.

reference_transcription: I AM NOT A MAN WHO CAN LIVE TWO LIVES HE WENT ON FEVERISHLY EACH LIFE SPOILS THE OTHER
corrected_asr_transcription: I am not a man who can live two lives," he went on feverishly. "Each life spoils the other."

asr_transcription.text: She bit her lip and looked down at her hands, which were clasped tightly in front of her.

reference_transcription: SHE BIT HER LIP AND LOOKED DOWN AT HER HANDS WHICH WERE CLASPED TIGHTLY IN FRONT OF HER
corrected_asr_transcription: She bit her lip and looked down at her hands, which were clasped tightly in front of her.

asr_transcription.text: Could you sit down and talk about it quietly, partly, as if I were a friend and not someone who had to be defied?

reference_transcription: COULD YOU COULD YOU SIT DOWN AND TALK ABOUT IT QUIETLY BARTLEY AS IF I WERE A FRIEND AND NOT SOME ONE WHO HAD TO BE DEFIED
corrected_asr_transcription: Could you sit down and talk about it quietly, partly, as if I were a friend and not someone who had to be defied?
